### Jesus' Great Compassion
Author: Emma Danzey
Site: Crosswalk
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/crosswalk-devo/jesus-great-compassion-the-crosswalk-devotional.html
Passage: Matthew 14:12-16
Points:
- Jesus showed authentic humanity in wanting solitary time to mourn the death of John the Baptist.
- Despite His deep personal sorrow, Jesus looked on the arriving crowd with divine compassion and healed them.
- When the disciples urged Him to dismiss the crowd, Jesus challenged them to take responsibility and feed the people.
- Following Christ requires stepping out in uncomfortable circumstances, where He rewards obedience with abundant provision.

### How Many Loaves Do You Have?
Author: Mike DeVries
Site: Crosswalk
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/homeword/how-many-loaves-do-you-have-homeword-november-18.html
Passage: Mark 6:38
Points:
- The disciples recognized the massive physical need around them but assumed they were powerless to address it.
- Jesus shifted their focus from their financial deficits to taking stock of the small resources already in their possession.
- Believers frequently wonder where God is during hardships, while God is inviting His followers to step in and help.
- Christ works through human surrender, using what we place in His hands to produce unexpected miracles.

### Day 156: Luke 9:10–17
Author: Beth Moore
Site: Crosswalk
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/plus/books/portraits-of-devotion/portraits-of-devotion-day-156-luke-9-1017.html
Passage: Luke 9:10-17
Points:
- Jesus understands our physical exhaustion and ministry fatigue, yet He generously welcomes needy people when interruptions occur.
- The Lord asks questions to reveal the boundaries of our faith and stretch our expectations of what He can provide.
- Christ does not bypass His disciples; He invites them to actively distribute the bread and participate in the miracle.
- When we bring every bit of our limited resources to Jesus, He multiplies them and leaves us with baskets full of leftovers.

### Multiplying Loaves and Fishes
Author: Ligonier Ministries
Site: Ligonier Ministries
URL: https://learn.ligonier.org/devotionals/multiplying-loaves-and-fishes
Passage: John 6:1-14
Points:
- Jesus questioned Philip to test whether he would look to divine power or rely solely on earthly arithmetic.
- The disciples saw the boy's five loaves and two small fish as completely insufficient for the massive crowd.
- Human limitations present no obstacle to Christ, who multiplied the meager food until every person was satisfied.
- Christ's willingness to feed a crowd following Him out of curiosity reassures believers that He will never abandon those who seek Him.
